Hello, I'm GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the Voucher Management Unit System so we can clearly understand the needs and define the right solution.

Before we begin, are you in line with the scope of this interview, or do you have different expectations for what we should cover?

Yes, I’m aligned with the scope. I’m here to help clarify how the voucher management unit works, what staff need to do in the system, and how we can improve the current manual processes. I’d expect us to focus on voucher creation and distribution, claims handling, reimbursement, validation, and reporting, including any fraud-checking needs.

Thank you for confirming the scope.

To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m speaking as someone from the program team at Marie Stopes International Uganda, closely involved with the voucher operations side. I understand the day-to-day workflow around distributing vouchers, tracking claims, and supporting reimbursements, so I can speak to what staff need from the system.
Thank you. Could you describe the current process or system you use for voucher creation, distribution, claims, reimbursement, and reporting?

Right now a lot of it is handled manually using paper records and spreadsheets, with different staff keeping track of sales, treatment claims, and reimbursements. Vouchers are distributed through program staff and service providers report back claims, which then have to be checked and validated before any payment is arranged. Reporting is mostly compiled after the fact, so it takes time and it’s hard to get a complete picture quickly.
Ok, what current processes do you want to change or improve, or what are the features you hope to get from this project?

We want to reduce the manual handling as much as possible, especially the back-and-forth in checking claims and preparing reimbursements. It would also help if the system could flag unusual or questionable claims so staff can review them sooner. Beyond that, we want better tracking and reporting so we can see program performance more clearly and with less delay.

So far, I understand the main features as: reducing manual handling, streamlining claim checking and reimbursement preparation, flagging unusual or questionable claims for review, and improving tracking and reporting.

Are there any other features you would like to see in this project?

Yes, I’d also want proper user access control so different staff can only do what they’re supposed to do, and an audit trail so we can see who created, edited, or approved each record. It would be useful to have search and filtering for vouchers and claims, because staff often need to find records quickly. If possible, simple dashboards or summaries for management would also be very helpful.
Based on your description, do you think integration with any existing tools or data sources, such as spreadsheets or other finance/reporting systems, should also be included?

Yes, I think that would be important. At the moment a lot of our information sits in spreadsheets, and finance also has its own processes for payments and reconciliation, so at minimum we should be able to import and export data cleanly. If there’s a way to connect to existing reporting or accounting tools later, that would be even better, but I’m not sure which exact systems would be in scope yet.
Thanks. Could you prioritize the main features we discussed in order of importance?

The first priority is claim validation and reimbursement handling, because that’s where most of the manual work and risk sit. After that, I’d put voucher creation and distribution, since those are the foundation of the program operations. Reporting and dashboards come next, followed by fraud flagging, search and filtering, and then integrations and other convenience features.
Please elaborate on what you want the claim validation and reimbursement handling feature to accomplish.

It should let staff review each claim against the voucher details and treatment rules, so they can confirm whether it is eligible before payment is arranged. The system should make it easy to approve, reject, or send back questionable claims for clarification, and then track the reimbursement status from validation through to payment. Ideally, it would also calculate or at least organize the amounts owed so finance can process them without redoing the checks manually.
Could you describe more about how staff currently validate claims and decide whether a claim is eligible or questionable?

Usually staff compare the claim documents with the voucher record and the service details to see whether the service was actually covered and whether the amounts look correct. They check things like whether the voucher was valid, whether the provider is approved, and whether the treatment matches what the program allows. If something doesn’t line up, or if the claim looks unusual compared with others, they will mark it for follow-up or reject it.
Could you describe the voucher creation and distribution feature in a bit more detail?

We need the system to let authorized staff create vouchers in batches or one by one, depending on the campaign or location. Each voucher should have a unique identifier and basic details like the beneficiary, service type, validity period, and status. Distribution should also be tracked so we know when a voucher was issued, to whom, and whether it was used, expired, or cancelled.
Could you elaborate on what you want the reporting and dashboard feature to accomplish?

It should give us a quick view of how the program is performing without having to compile everything manually. We’d want summaries like how many vouchers were issued and used, how many claims were submitted, approved, rejected, or pending, and how much reimbursement is outstanding or already paid. For managers, it would also help to show trends over time and highlight unusual patterns that may need attention.
Could you describe more about the fraud flagging feature—what kinds of unusual or questionable claims should the system detect or highlight?

We’d want it to flag things like duplicate claims, claims for vouchers that were already used or expired, unusually high amounts, and repeated submissions from the same provider or beneficiary in a short period. It should also highlight cases where the service type doesn’t match the voucher, or where the claim falls outside the expected dates. I wouldn’t expect it to automatically accuse anyone, just to draw attention to records that need closer review.
Who else do you think has valuable insights into the project, and whose needs need to be considered, and why?

Definitely the finance team, because they handle the reimbursements and need the records to be clear enough for payment processing and audit. Service providers also matter since they submit claims and need the process to be straightforward and transparent. Program managers and field staff are important too because they monitor performance and work with beneficiaries on the ground, so the system has to fit their daily workflow.
Thank you for the detailed input. To help define success for this system, what would make you consider the deployment successful?

We’d consider it successful if it reduces the amount of manual checking and paperwork, and if staff can process vouchers and claims faster with fewer errors. It should also improve visibility, so managers can trust the reports and quickly spot questionable claims or payment delays. If the people using it adopt it without too much trouble and it supports accurate reimbursements, that would be a strong sign it’s working well.

To summarize, we discussed reducing manual handling, claim validation and reimbursement tracking, voucher creation and distribution, reporting and dashboards, fraud-flagging, search/filtering, access control, audit trails, and import/export integration needs. Is there anything else you would like to add?

One important thing is data security and confidentiality, because we’re dealing with beneficiary and provider information. I’d also want the system to be reliable when the internet is unstable, since some staff may be working in areas with poor connectivity. Other than that, I think the main needs we discussed cover what we require.
